title: Researchers develop a record-efficiency white OLED that uses a single MR-TADF emitter molecule
content: Researchers from China's Jilin University and Ji Hua Laboratory have developed a warm-white OLED that uses a single light-emitting molecule (a single dopant). The new emitter, called Th-DBN, is a multi-resonance TADF (MR-TADF) material that emits blue-green light on its own, and orange-yellow light when two molecules stack together. title: Kyulux raises $53.7 million in a Series D round backed by LG Display and Samsung, signs a joint development agreement with LGD
content: Japan-based TADF and Hyperfluorescence OLED emitter developer Kyulux has raised 8.5 billion Yen (about $53.7 million USD) in a Series D funding round, which values the company at around $272 million. Investors include SMBC Capital Partners (part of Japan's SMBC Group), Korean private equity firm H&Q and BNW. title: Quantum computing company IonQ raises 2026 revenue forecast above US$500 million on commercial growth
content: IonQ raised its 2026 revenue forecast to US$505 million-US$515 million after reporting record third-quarter revenue of US$173.8 million, as its quantum computing business expanded across data centers, defense programs, and enterprise deployments. The results marked a 336% year-over-year increase and reflected the company’s shift from laboratory research toward commercial quantum applications in the US and global markets.

title: Global AI memory crunch drives Taiwan to launch advanced memory initiative
content: The boom in AI demand has triggered a global memory crunch, creating persistent supply shortages and price hikes. The market is currently dominated by Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, and Micron Technology. While China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has expanded its mass-production capabilities rapidly, US export controls and cybersecurity concerns continue to prevent it from competing directly in the US against American and South Korean rivals.
